questions.q: A validation rule's Error Condition Formula evaluates to TRUE. What happens?
options: The record saves and a warning is logged
The save is blocked and the error message is shown
The field referenced in the formula is cleared
The record is saved to a recycle bin for review
questions.explain: TRUE means the bad condition was met, so the save is blocked and the configured error message displays at the chosen Error Location.

questions.q: Which function would you use to check whether a picklist field's value is 'Closed Lost'?
options: ISBLANK()
REGEX()
ISPICKVAL()
PRIORVALUE()
questions.explain: ISPICKVAL() compares a picklist field's current value against a specified option, exactly this kind of check.

questions.q: Which statement about who a validation rule applies to is correct?
options: It applies to everyone, including System Administrators, unless the formula itself builds in an exception
Administrators are automatically exempt from all validation rules
It only applies to users with the 'Standard User' profile
It applies only during bulk Data Loader imports
questions.explain: There is no built-in administrator exception. Any exception, such as skipping enforcement for a System Administrator profile, has to be written into the formula itself.

questions.q: Which of these is something a validation rule CANNOT do?
options: Block a record from being saved
Reference the current and prior value of a changed field
Change or set the value of a field
Display a custom error message at a specific field
questions.explain: A validation rule can only allow or block a save — it has no ability to write or change a field's value. That's a job for a formula field, Flow, or Apex.

questions.q: A rule's formula references StageName, Amount, and Close_Reason__c, and the error only makes sense when all three combine in a specific way. What's generally the better practice versus cramming it into one dense formula?
options: Write several smaller, clearly named rules instead of one dense rule
Move the logic into a dashboard filter
Disable the fields from being edited
Always put the formula in the field's help text instead
questions.explain: Because one rule evaluates the whole record at once and can only show one message, most experienced admins split complex requirements into several small, well-named rules rather than one hard-to-read rule.
